title: Marketing psychology: mental models for understanding buyers and influencing behavior
summary: Corey's open-source AI skill cataloging mental models for marketing: foundational thinking models, buyer psychology, persuasion, pricing psychology, behavior design and growth dynamics. It pairs each model with a concrete marketing application and a quick-reference table of challenges to models.

principles.text: Find and fix the single bottleneck before optimizing anywhere else.
principles.quote: If your funnel converts well but traffic is low, more conversion optimization won't help. Fix the traffic bottleneck first.

principles.text: Zoom out before optimizing: make sure you're on the right channel before tuning details.
principles.quote: Optimizing email subject lines (local) won't help if email isn't the right channel (global). Zoom out before zooming in.

principles.text: Focus on the vital few channels, customers and content driving most results; cut the rest.
principles.quote: Find the 20% of channels, customers, or content driving 80% of results. Cut or reduce the rest.

principles.text: Lean on proven fundamentals over trendy tactics, while keeping a small budget for experiments.
principles.quote: Put 80% of budget into proven channels, 20% into experimental bets. Avoid moderate-risk, moderate-reward middle.

principles.text: Limit choices and reduce friction: fewer options, one clear CTA, fewer fields, simple pricing tiers.
principles.quote: Limit options. Three pricing tiers beat seven. Recommend a single "best for most" option.

principles.text: Behavior needs motivation, ability and a prompt together; design for all three and make the first step trivially easy.
principles.quote: High motivation but hard to do = won't happen. Easy to do but no prompt = won't happen. Design for all three.
